title: Return and Down pressed before results arrive act on the previous rows
problem: The manual promises 'Return searches right away and moves into the results, selecting the first one' (docs/manual.md:324). Results arrive at least 50 ms after the last keystroke (debounce, src/finder/mod.rs:1391-1395) and up to the time limit for a contents search (default 5 s, crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:378) or while a temporary index builds. Until then `self.rows` still holds the folder listing or the previous query's results. `InputEvent::PressEnter` calls `run_search(false, cx)`, which only spawns the search (mod.rs:1390-1434), and on the next line tests `if !self.rows.is_empty()`, focuses the files and selects row 0 of those old rows (mod.rs:1308-1318). When the real results land, `rebuild_rows` remaps the selection by path (mod.rs:1268-1269), so it either vanishes (keyboard in the files with nothing selected) or sticks to an item that is no longer the top hit, which a second Return then opens. Down has the same stale check (src/finder/toolbar.rs:449-460). In an empty folder Return does nothing at all. The existing test only passes because `type_text` settles before the key (tests/finder.rs:86-89; tests/common/mod.rs:282-286, 430-434). Related: Return always calls `run_search(false)` even when results are current, which restarts a multi-second contents search just to move focus (mod.rs:1310).
proposal: In src/finder/mod.rs add `enter_results: Option<u64>`, the search generation that should take the keyboard. In `on_search_event`'s PressEnter arm: read the field's current value (`state.read(cx).value()`) and call `set_query(value, true, cx)` so a not-yet-delivered Change cannot matter. If `self.searching` is false the rows already belong to the query: do not re-run; focus the files and select and scroll to row 0 as now. If a request is in flight, call `run_search(false, cx)` only to skip the debounce and set `enter_results = Some(self.search_gen)`. In the completion closure of `run_search` (mod.rs:1421-1433), after `rebuild_rows`, when `enter_results == Some(generation)` and rows are non-empty: `selection.select_only(0)`, `scroll_to(0)`, `selection_changed`, give the files the keyboard, clear the flag; when the awaited results are empty, drop the flag and leave focus in the field. That closure has no `Window`, so either spawn the search with `cx.spawn_in(window, ..)`/`update_in` when started from the field (pattern in src/finder/trash.rs:61-64) or consume a `focus_results` flag at the top of `render`. (Simpler variant from the second reviewer: call `focus_files` and clear the selection at once and only select row 0 on completion; needs no window but leaves the keyboard in an empty file area when nothing matches.) Clear the flag in `set_query` when the query changes, in `end_search`, and when the search field regains focus. Route the Down handler in src/finder/toolbar.rs:449-460 through the same deferred path while `this.searching`. Update the hint in src/finder/dialogs.rs (about line 1003) and docs/manual.md:964-969. Escape in the empty field is covered by the escape-ends-search candidate.
original_test_plan: Headless UI tests in tests/finder.rs: `ui.click("search")`, then in one window step without settling between them `ui.window(|w, cx| { w.input("roadmap", cx); w.press("enter", cx); })`, then `ui.settle()`; assert `ui.files_focused()` and `ui.selected() == ["Roadmap.md"]` (today the selection is empty: Budget.csv, row 0 of the folder listing, was selected and then remapped away). Same with `w.press("down", cx)` and with the query `atlas` asserting `ui.selected() == [ui.names()[0]]`. Keep the settled-typing tests green (tests/finder.rs:67-99, 86-89, 250-263; tests/controls.rs:317-325).
original_risks: If the awaited results are empty, focus should stay in (or return to) the field; make sure the flag is dropped then. The flag must not select row 0 after the user has already clicked a different row. Anyone using Return as a manual refresh loses that (Cmd+R still re-runs).

verifier.claim_check:
The described behaviour is real; I could not refute it.

- Return: src/finder/mod.rs:1308-1318. `PressEnter` calls `run_search(false, cx)`, which only bumps `search_gen`, sets `searching = true` and spawns (mod.rs:1360-1390). It then tests `!self.rows.is_empty()` against rows that are still the folder listing or the previous query's results, focuses the files and selects row 0 of them.
- Results land later (mod.rs:1421-1433): `rebuild_rows` remaps the selection by path (mod.rs:1268-1269, src/model.rs:324-336). A stale row 0 either vanishes, leaving the keyboard in the files with nothing selected, or sticks to an item that is no longer the top hit.
- Down: src/finder/toolbar.rs:449-460 has the same stale `!this.rows.is_empty()` check.
- Empty folder: rows are empty, so Return moves nothing, and the completion closure never moves focus.
- Worse than the candidate says: a quick Return, Return opens the stale item at once. After the first Return the files have focus with stale row 0 selected, and `enter` there is `OpenSelected` (src/actions.rs:184 -> mod.rs:1977-1990). In the fixture that would be Budget.csv, or a folder navigation that ends the search.
- Restart on Return is true, and costlier than stated: `engine.grep` is a blocking call inside `background_spawn`, so dropping `search_task` does not stop it. A Return during a contents search leaves the old grep running to its time limit (config.rs:378, 5 s) beside the new one.
- Timing: 50 ms debounce (mod.rs:1391-1395) plus search time for a warm name search, so the race is narrow there. It is wide for contents searches, temporary indexes (engine.rs:495) and the launch-time index build (CHANGELOG.md:188, "can still wait a few seconds").
- Not intentional, not already handled: docs/manual.md:324 and :968 promise "moves into the results, selecting the first one". CHANGELOG.md has nothing on it. `InputEvent::Focus | Blur` are ignored (mod.rs:1319).
- Tests pin only the settled case: tests/finder.rs:86-89 and 250-257, tests/controls.rs:317-319, all through `type_text`/`press`, which settle (tests/common/mod.rs:282-286, 426-434).
- Precedent: the same class of bug was fixed for Go to Folder's Tab (src/finder/go_to.rs:81-90, tests/controls.rs:943-962).

Where the proposal is wrong or incomplete:
1. Keying the flag to one generation, and dropping it on empty results, breaks the longest wait. During the launch-time index build the first response comes back at once with `indexing = true` and few or no rows, then mod.rs:1435-1457 re-runs under a new generation. `poll_index_status` (mod.rs:1509), watcher reloads and settings changes also bump the generation.
2. "A not-yet-delivered Change" cannot happen for Return: `Change` and `PressEnter` are both `cx.emit` effects, delivered in order. It can happen for Down in the proposed one-closure test: the `capture_key_down` handler runs during dispatch, before the queued `Change` is delivered (effects flush only when the outermost update ends, gpui app.rs:1390-1395). `this.searching` is still false and `query` still empty there, so "route Down through the deferred path while `this.searching`" would not fire and that test would fail.
3. It still restarts a request that is already running.
4. With a Nushell filter on, rows after a search completes are filtered by the previous keep-set until the filter task finishes (src/finder/filter.rs:96-109, 134-147). Consuming the flag at search completion can select a row that then disappears.
5. "Clear when the field regains focus" is the wrong guard for the deferred variant, where the field never loses focus.
6. Effort is M, not S. The dialogs.rs:1003 hint stays accurate and needs no edit.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Corrected plan. All of it is cross-platform code in src/finder.

**1. State (mod.rs, beside `searching`/`search_gen` at :303-305)**
- Add `enter_results: Option<AnyWindowHandle>`: Return or Down was pressed before the results for what is typed were in; holds the window to focus in.
- Do not key it to a generation. Stale generations never deliver (mod.rs:1423), so "the next results delivered" always belong to the current query.

**2. One shared entry point for Return and Down**
`fn move_into_results(&mut self, window, cx) -> bool`:
- Sync from the field first: `set_query(self.search_input.read(cx).value().to_string(), true, cx)`. It is a no-op when unchanged (early return at mod.rs:1325), and it makes the Down capture handler correct even when a `Change` is still queued.
- If `!self.searching` and `!self.is_filtering()`: the rows are current. Keep today's behaviour: if rows are non-empty, `focus_files`, and if the selection is empty `select_only(0)`, `scroll_to(0)`, `selection_changed`, `cx.notify()`. Do not call `run_search`.
- Otherwise: `self.selection.clear()`, `self.enter_results = Some(window.window_handle())`, leave focus in the field.
- Re-run without the debounce only while the request is still in its 50 ms wait. Track that with a `search_waiting: bool`, set from `debounce` in `run_search` and cleared after the timer in a generation-guarded update. Never restart a running request.
- Return true when the key was handled, so Down can `stop_propagation` in the deferred case too.

**3. Call sites**
- mod.rs:1308-1318: the `PressEnter` arm becomes `self.move_into_results(window, cx);`.
- toolbar.rs:449-460: on "down", call `move_into_results` and stop propagation when it returns true (keep letting Down through when there is nothing to wait for and no rows, as today).
- Same capture handler: any key other than Return or Down sets `this.enter_results = None`, so editing the query cancels the pending move.

**4. Delivery**
`fn take_enter_results(&mut self, more_coming: bool) -> Option<AnyWindowHandle>`:
- Returns None and keeps the flag while `self.searching || self.filtering`, or while rows are empty and `more_coming` (the `stats.indexing` retry).
- Otherwise takes the flag.

Call it in two places:
- The `run_search` completion closure (mod.rs:1421-1433), after `rebuild_rows`; return it alongside `retry`.
- The filter completion (filter.rs:134-147), after `rebuild_rows`.

Both closures have only an `AsyncApp`. With the handle, do `cx.update_window(handle, |_, window, cx| this.update(cx, |this, cx| this.finish_enter(window, cx)))`. This needs no change to `run_search`'s signature or its ~15 callers, which rules out the `spawn_in` rewrite. The "consume in render" variant would misfire for a background tab.

`finish_enter`:
- Do nothing unless the search field still holds focus: `self.search_input.read(cx).focus_handle(cx).is_focused(window)`. This covers a dialog opened, a row clicked, or a tab switched in the meantime.
- If rows are empty, leave focus in the field.
- Otherwise `focus_files`, select row 0 if the selection is empty (the gallery may already have picked it, mod.rs:1283), `scroll_to(0)`, `selection_changed`, `cx.notify()`.

**5. Clearing**
- In `set_query` whenever the query actually changes. This covers `end_search`, navigation and smart folders.
- Optionally on `InputEvent::Blur` (mod.rs:1319).

**6. Docs**
- docs/manual.md:324: add one sentence, e.g. "If the results aren't in yet, Return and Down Arrow wait for them."
- CHANGELOG.md: a "Fixed" entry under [Unreleased].
- docs/manual.md:964-969 and dialogs.rs:1003 can stay.

**Pitfalls**
- `select_only(0)` ignores collapsed groups. That is existing behaviour; leave it.
- Do not drop the flag on an empty response with `indexing = true`.
- Rejected: the "focus the files at once, select later" variant. It strands the keyboard in an empty file area on no results, and a second Return there is `OpenSelected`.
verifier.test_plan:
Headless UI tests in tests/finder.rs, next to `type_into_the_search_field_and_down_arrow` (line 249).

Helpers: `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.click("search")`, `ui.window(|w, cx| ..)` with `use gpui_kit::test::TestWindowExt as _;` (the pattern at tests/controls.rs:943-957), `ui.settle()`, `ui.files_focused()`, `ui.selected()`, `ui.names()`, `ui.folder()`, `ui.system_calls()`, and `ui.window(|w, cx| w.has_focused_input(cx))`.

Use a separate `ui.window` call for each key, with no `settle` between them. Effects then flush between keys as they do for real key events, while spawned and background work stays parked until `settle` (the same reliance as `click_without_settling`, tests/common/mod.rs:331-337).

1. Return before results
   - `ui.window(|w, cx| w.input("roadmap", cx)); ui.window(|w, cx| w.press("enter", cx));`
   - Before settling: `!ui.files_focused()` and `ui.selected().is_empty()`. Today Budget.csv is selected and the files have focus.
   - After `ui.settle()`: `ui.files_focused()` and `ui.selected() == ["Roadmap.md"]`. Today the selection is empty.
2. Down before results: the same with `w.press("down", cx)`. Also the one-closure form `{ w.input(..); w.press("down", cx); }`, which pins the sync-from-field step.
3. Return, Return before results: three window steps, then `settle`. Assert no `SystemCall::Open` in `ui.system_calls()`, `ui.folder()` unchanged, and `ui.selected() == ["Roadmap.md"]`. Today Budget.csv is opened.
4. No matches: input "zzqq-nothing", Return, settle. Assert `!ui.files_focused()`, the input still has focus, and `ui.names().is_empty()`.
5. Typing after Return cancels: input "road", Return, input "map", settle. Assert focus is still in the field, the query is "roadmap", and the selection is empty.
6. Query "atlas", Return unsettled, settle: `ui.selected() == [ui.names()[0]]`.

Must stay green: tests/finder.rs:67-99 and 250-263, tests/controls.rs:304-326 (the settled path), tests/controls.rs:1453-1456 (search with a filter on).

Not covered: the indexing-retry path, which the harness cannot stage deterministically. Keep `take_enter_results(more_coming)` a small pure-ish method so it can be read and checked directly. Nothing here was run; the review was read-only.
verifier.risks:
- Focus now moves when results arrive, possibly seconds after Return (contents search, index build). It must be cancelled by any edit or other key in the field and skipped unless the field still holds focus, or it will steal the keyboard from a dialog, a clicked row or further typing.
- A flag that is never cleared would grab focus on some later, unrelated re-run (watcher reload, settings change). Clear it on query change and consume it exactly once.
- Return no longer re-runs a settled search, and no longer restarts a running one. Anyone using Return as a refresh loses that; Cmd+R still re-runs (mod.rs:1199-1204), and the manual's "searches right away" stays true for the debounce.
- `cx.update_window` from the completion closure adds a window hop. It must tolerate a closed window (`.ok()`), and must not run inside another update of the same Finder.
- With a Nushell filter on, delivery must wait for the filter task, or the selected row can still vanish.
- The fast path (warm name search) only hits the race within roughly 50-100 ms of the last keystroke, so most of the benefit is on slow searches and the Return, Return hazard.
